newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan have denied rumours that the government will sack the central bank governor for failing to lower the discount rate. Though he admits that he feels the Bank of Thailand's decision to maintain the discount rate and restructure the minimum retail rate calculation formula are not the right strategies for reviving the sagging economy, Chavalit says that the government will stay out of the central bank's decisions and the the rumours are insubstantial. (THE NATION)

- The judiciary committee investigating a senior judge for granting bail to suspected drug trafficker Li Yun-chung may decide not to question a key witness because he would not give any useful information. A source in the judiciary says instead of questioning this particular witness, identified only as "Phuek", the committee will give information about the man's telephone communications with others to the police. (BANGKOK POST)

- Public Relations Department chief Chan Poonsombat has been transferred to an inactive post at the Prime Minister's Office after his longstanding rift with Piyanat Watcharaporn boiled over. Piyanat, a Prime Minister's Office minister, cites Chan's decision to promote two middle-ranking officials against his standing policy as a reason for his transfer order. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Cabinet has approved a budget plan for construction of the Second Bangkok International Airport at Nong Ngu Hao of 68.83 billion baht after a reduction from 97.3 billion baht. The reduction will affect the foundation work as the original budget of 11.6 billion baht has already been reduced to 8.5 billion baht. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Cabinet has passed a proposal to establish free trade zones to boost key export-oriented industries. Industry Minister Korn Dabbaransi says industries located in these zones will enjoy certain Board of Investment privileges including tax holidays on machinery imports and corporate tax exemptions for a set period. (BANGKOK POST)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has ordered the creation of a task force to consider ways to promote the electronics industry and recommend whether government agencies should have an equity participation in electronics projects. The task force is another follow-up action from the Export Summit. (THE NATION)
